subject: Compiler & System Software
question: The main difference between a compiler and an interpreter is that a compiler:
option_a: Translates the whole source program to machine code in one pass before execution
option_b: Executes source statements one by one without producing a standalone object file
option_c: Only checks syntax and does nothing else
option_d: Is used only for web pages
explanation: A compiler translates the entire program into machine code (object file) then executes it; an interpreter translates and executes line by line.

subject: Compiler & System Software
question: Which is the correct order of the main phases of a compiler?
option_a: Lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic analysis, intermediate code, optimization, code generation
option_b: Syntax, lexical, semantic, optimization, code generation
explanation: Standard phases: lexical (tokens) -> syntax (parse tree) -> semantic (type checks) -> intermediate code -> optimization -> target code.

question: A grammar G = (N, T, P, S) - what does P represent?
explanation: P is the set of production rules (rewriting rules). N are non-terminals, T terminals, S the start symbol.

subject: Compiler & System Software
question: LL parsing is a top-down method that:
option_a: Starts from the start symbol and expands according to lookahead tokens
option_b: Reduces the input from right to left
option_c: Builds trees from leaves to root by shift-reduce
explanation: LL = Left-to-right scan, Leftmost derivation; it predicts expansions from the start symbol. LR/bottom-up parsing reduces input to the start symbol.
